project.name: vps-infrastructure
project.description: Ansible Infrastructure-as-Code for a two-VPS setup: a main public web host fronted by Traefik (with Let's Encrypt) and a dedicated Jenkins CI/CD host that builds container images and deploys back to the main VPS. Secrets are stored in ansible-vault.

nodes.name: .ansible-lint
nodes.summary: Ansible-lint configuration using the 'min' profile with intentional skips (command-instead-of-module, no-changed-when, risky-file-permissions) and mocks the jenkins role to keep CI tolerant of pragmatic Ansible patterns.

nodes.name: ansible.cfg
nodes.summary: Ansible runtime defaults wiring inventory, role path, jsonfile fact caching (1h TTL), SSH pipelining/ControlMaster, and sudo privilege escalation for all playbook executions.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Project-specific guidance for Claude Code agents covering repo topology, common commands, architectural conventions, role ordering constraints, and gotchas like the Miplata pull-tolerant deploy pattern.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Human-facing project overview describing the two-VPS Ansible setup, role-to-service mapping for both hosts, usage commands, repository layout, and the Jenkins CI flow.

nodes.name: Jenkinsfile
nodes.summary: Declarative Jenkins pipeline running galaxy install, ansible-lint, syntax check, dry run, deploy, and health-check stages, injecting vault password and SSH key from credentials and scrubbing the temp vault file on every exit.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses withCredentials + a temp .vault_pass_tmp file pattern so the vault password never touches disk outside the build workspace; an always-block guarantees cleanup.

nodes.name: playbook.yml
nodes.summary: Main VPS deploy playbook applying eleven roles in dependency-sensitive order (base, docker, traefik, dns, vaultwarden, monitoring, zot, miplata, metabase, llm_inference, categorizer) and writing a node_exporter textfile deploy marker.
nodes.languageNotes: Role ordering is load-bearing — traefik must precede any role that joins the proxy network.

nodes.name: jenkins-playbook.yml
nodes.summary: Jenkins-host deploy playbook applying the hardened baseline (base, docker, traefik) plus the jenkins role and observability_agent that pushes metrics/logs back to the main VPS.

nodes.name: requirements.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible Galaxy requirements pinning community.docker >=3.0.0, the only external collection needed for docker_compose_v2 / docker_network modules used across roles.

nodes.name: inventory.yml
nodes.summary: Two-host inventory defining 'vps' (ubuntu user) and 'jenkins' (root user), with ansible_host addresses sourced from vault variables so the repo is safe to publish.

nodes.name: all.yml
nodes.summary: Project-wide variable store: domain/subdomain patterns, Docker network list, SSH/UFW/fail2ban defaults, and pinned container image tags for Traefik, PowerDNS, Vaultwarden, the full observability stack, Jenkins, Zot, Miplata, Metabase, llama.cpp, and the categorizer.
nodes.languageNotes: First place to look when changing any service hostname or pinned image version — every role reads from here.

nodes.name: jenkins.yml
nodes.summary: Jenkins-host overrides allowing root login, narrowing UFW to SSH/HTTP/HTTPS (no DNS ports), and renaming the Traefik dashboard host to traefik-ci.<web_subdomain>.

nodes.name: vps.yml
nodes.summary: Main VPS host overrides binding ansible_host and vps_public_ip to the vault-supplied IP so other roles can reference the public address.

nodes.name: vault.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible-vault AES256-encrypted secret store holding all passwords, SSH deploy keys, OAuth credentials, bearer tokens, and identifying values (IPs, domain, ACME email) consumed by every role at template-render time.
nodes.languageNotes: Opaque ciphertext on disk — referenced via vars_files in both playbooks and unlocked by .vault_pass or Jenkins credential injection.

nodes.name: vault.yml.example
nodes.summary: Plaintext template enumerating every vault variable the project expects (PowerDNS, Vaultwarden, Grafana OAuth, Jenkins deploy keys, Miplata, Zot htpasswd, Metabase, categorizer, plus IPs/domain), used for first-time vault bootstrap.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Base role defaults listing required apt packages (ufw, fail2ban, curl, git, htop, unattended-upgrades) and the conservative PermitRootLogin=no SSH default that host_vars override on the Jenkins host.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Base role handlers restarting ssh, fail2ban, and systemd-journald when their respective config templates or drop-ins change.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Base role task list installing core packages, enabling unattended-upgrades, applying SSH hardening, configuring UFW (including a narrow Docker-bridge rule to reach host node_exporter on :9100), installing journald limits, and configuring fail2ban.
nodes.languageNotes: The 172.16.0.0/12 UFW rule for node_exporter is deliberately scoped to Docker's reserved range to avoid public exposure — do not widen it.

nodes.name: journald-observability.conf
nodes.summary: systemd-journald drop-in capping disk usage (500M system / 100M runtime), enforcing 14-day retention with daily rotation, and rate-limiting to keep Alloy's journal reader bounded.

nodes.name: jail.local.j2
nodes.summary: fail2ban jail.local template wiring tunable bantime/findtime/maxretry defaults and an sshd jail with UFW as the ban action, pulling all thresholds from group_vars.

nodes.name: sshd-hardening.conf.j2
nodes.summary: sshd drop-in template enforcing per-host root-login policy, max auth tries, login grace, no X11 forwarding, an AllowUsers allowlist, and keepalive timeouts.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Docker role default selecting docker-compose-plugin as the Compose v2 package to install alongside docker-ce.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Docker role handler restarting the docker service when /etc/docker/daemon.json changes.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Docker role tasks installing prerequisites, idempotently adding the Docker apt repo (guarded by a docker --version probe), installing docker-ce + compose plugin, configuring the daemon, adding ansible_user to the docker group, and creating the shared docker_networks list.
nodes.languageNotes: GPG key + repo add steps are gated on docker_installed.rc != 0 so re-runs are no-ops on hosts that already have Docker.

nodes.name: daemon.json.j2
nodes.summary: Docker daemon.json template capping container log files to 10MB with a 3-file rotation under the default json-file driver.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines the default install directory (`traefik_dir`) for the Traefik role, used by tasks to know where to place compose files and ACME storage.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines the `restart traefik` handler that runs `docker compose restart` when tasks notify a config change.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Provisions Traefik: creates `/opt/traefik`, copies the static config and nginx socket proxy, renders the compose file, ensures `acme.json` is 0600, and starts the stack.

nodes.name: nginx-docker-proxy.conf
nodes.summary: Nginx configuration for a read-only Docker socket proxy that exposes only the endpoints Traefik needs (containers, services, networks).
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the docker-socket-proxy pattern by whitelisting specific URI paths and rejecting all others.

nodes.name: nginx.conf
nodes.summary: Top-level nginx configuration wrapper for the docker socket proxy sidecar — sets worker processes, events, and includes the http server block.

nodes.name: traefik.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Traefik static configuration template: defines entrypoints (web/websecure), the Docker provider via the socket proxy, Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 ACME resolver, and access logging.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Compose stack rendering Traefik plus its nginx docker-socket-proxy sidecar; binds ports 80/443, mounts `acme.json`, and attaches to the shared `proxy` network for label-based routing.
nodes.languageNotes: The nginx sidecar fronts /var/run/docker.sock so Traefik never reads the host socket directly — a defense-in-depth pattern.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines `dns_dir` default (typically `/opt/dns`) consumed by the DNS role's tasks and templates.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines the `restart dns` handler that restarts the PowerDNS compose stack when configuration changes.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Provisions the authoritative PowerDNS server: creates `/opt/dns`, renders `pdns.conf`/`.env`/compose templates, then brings up the DNS container stack.

nodes.name: env.j2
nodes.summary: Renders the `.env` file injecting PowerDNS API key and database credentials from vault into the compose stack.

nodes.name: pdns.conf.j2
nodes.summary: PowerDNS authoritative server configuration template: enables the SQLite backend, REST API for `pdnsutil`-style updates, and webserver/API key auth.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Compose stack rendering the PowerDNS container with UDP/TCP 53 published, SQLite volume mounted, and Traefik labels exposing the API on an internal hostname.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines `vaultwarden_dir` default install path used by the Vaultwarden role's tasks and compose template.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Provisions Vaultwarden: creates the install and data directories, renders `.env` and `docker-compose.yml` from templates, then starts the password-manager stack.

nodes.name: env.j2
nodes.summary: Renders the Vaultwarden `.env` with admin token and domain settings sourced from vault and group_vars.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Compose stack rendering the Vaultwarden container with persistent data volume and Traefik labels for TLS termination on the configured subdomain.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines defaults for the Zot OCI registry role: install directory, data directory for image blobs, and the Zot container image tag.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defines the `restart zot` handler that restarts the Zot registry stack when its config or htpasswd file changes.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Provisions the self-hosted Zot OCI registry consumed by the Jenkins build pipeline: renders config/htpasswd, brings up the compose stack, registers a PowerDNS A record, and waits for the HTTP endpoint to be ready.

nodes.name: config.json.j2
nodes.summary: Zot registry configuration template: defines storage paths, htpasswd auth, HTTP listener, and any sync/extension settings.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Compose stack rendering the Zot OCI registry container with bind-mounted config, htpasswd, data volume, and Traefik labels for TLS-terminated public access.

nodes.name: htpasswd.j2
nodes.summary: Renders the htpasswd credential file used by Zot for HTTP basic-auth, sourced from vault-encrypted username/bcrypt-hash variables.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Default variables for the Miplata role: install directory under /opt/miplata, uploads path bind-mounted into the API container, Postgres user/db names, and the UID/GID the NestJS container runs as so the host-side uploads dir matches.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible task list that provisions Miplata: creates dirs, renders .env and compose file, logs into the Zot registry, ensures the DNS A record, tolerantly pulls images (skips `up` on a fresh VPS when Jenkins hasn't built them yet), and idempotently provisions a read-only PG user and a postgres-exporter role.
nodes.languageNotes: The `failed_when: false` on docker compose pull + `when: miplata_pull.rc == 0` guards are intentional — they make the role idempotent across first-boot (no images in Zot) and steady-state.

nodes.name: env.j2
nodes.summary: Jinja2 template rendering Miplata's runtime `.env`: Postgres credentials, JWT secret, BullMQ/Redis settings, uploads path, and tracing OTEL endpoints into the observability network.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose template defining the Miplata stack: Postgres + Redis on an internal network, the NestJS API (uploads bind-mounted), nginx Web exposed via Traefik labels, plus postgres- and redis-exporters joined to the observability network.
nodes.languageNotes: API image is pulled from the self-hosted Zot registry (built by a separate Jenkins job, not by this role).

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Default variables for the Metabase role: install dir, Metabase application-DB user/name, and initial admin user identity (name, email, site name) used to bootstrap the instance via the Setup API.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible tasks that deploy Metabase: render .env and compose, ensure DNS, start the stack, wait for the API to be healthy, complete first-time admin setup over HTTPS, and register Miplata's Postgres as a Metabase data source via the read-only `metabase_ro` role.
nodes.languageNotes: Setup is fully automated through Metabase's REST API; subsequent runs are no-ops because `has-user-setup` short-circuits the setup task.

nodes.name: env.j2
nodes.summary: Jinja2 template rendering Metabase's `.env`: Postgres app-DB credentials and JVM/site settings for the Metabase container.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose template for Metabase: dedicated Postgres app-DB on an internal-only network plus the Metabase app exposed via Traefik. Metabase also joins the `miplata_db` network so it can query Miplata's Postgres as a read-only data source.
nodes.languageNotes: Metabase joining `miplata_db` is what enables it to read from miplata-postgres using the `metabase_ro` user.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Default variables for the Categorizer role: install dir, Postgres user/db with pgvector, container UID/GID, app port and thread count, plus mem/cpuset limits that constrain the AI service to a dedicated CPU set.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible tasks that deploy the AI categorizer service: dirs, .env, compose, DNS, bootstrap-tolerant pull from Zot, start stack, and enable the pgvector extension in the dedicated Postgres once the stack is up.

nodes.name: env.j2
nodes.summary: Jinja2 env template wiring the Categorizer to its own Postgres+pgvector, a read-only DSN into Miplata's DB for training data, the internal llama-server LLM endpoint, an API bearer token (enforced by a Traefik middleware), and OTLP tracing to Alloy.
nodes.languageNotes: Critical cross-role wiring lives here: `LLM_BASE_URL` points at `llama-server` (llm_inference role) and `MIPLATA_RO_DATABASE_URL` points at `miplata-postgres` using the RO user provisioned by the miplata role.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose template for the Categorizer stack: a dedicated Postgres on `categorizer_net`, plus the API container joined to four networks (proxy, categorizer_net, miplata_db, observability) and protected by a Traefik bearer-token middleware. mem_limit/cpuset bound its CPU footprint.
nodes.languageNotes: Cross-stack dependency on llama-server is intentionally not declared via depends_on (Compose can't model cross-project deps); the app retries on startup instead.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Default variables for the llm_inference role: install/models dirs, GGUF model filename and `LLM_MODEL` id, llama.cpp tuning (ctx size, threads, parallel slots, temp, top-k, seed), and container mem/cpuset constraints plus the served port.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible tasks that deploy llama-server: create dirs (models dir operator-owned for scp), render .env and compose, warn if the GGUF file isn't yet on disk, then start the stack. Unlike miplata/categorizer the image comes from public ghcr.io so a pull failure is a real error.

nodes.name: env.j2
nodes.summary: Jinja2 env template that translates the role's defaults into llama.cpp `LLAMA_ARG_*` environment variables (model path, ctx size, threads, parallel slots, port, slot/webui toggles).

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose template for the llama-server container: joined to `categorizer_net` (serves /v1/chat/completions to the categorizer) and the observability network (scraped for /metrics + /health). Models dir mounted read-only.
nodes.languageNotes: No Traefik labels — this service is intentionally internal-only. Reachable only on `categorizer_net`.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Minimal default variables for the Jenkins role: install dir (/opt/jenkins) and the data dir bind-mounted into the container as JENKINS_HOME.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Single Ansible handler that restarts the Jenkins compose stack — triggered when the JCasC config file changes so Jenkins re-reads its declarative configuration on next boot.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Ansible tasks that build and run a containerized Jenkins: disable any pre-existing systemd Jenkins, create dirs, discover the host's docker GID, copy Dockerfile+plugins.txt and build the local `jenkins-ansible:latest` image, deploy SSH keys + known_hosts, render JCasC and compose, start the stack, and install a weekly docker-prune cron.
nodes.languageNotes: The role grafts the host's docker GID into the container so the jenkins user can talk to the bind-mounted docker.sock — this is what enables Jenkins to build images on the host.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-step Dockerfile extending `jenkins/jenkins:lts-jdk21` with Ansible (via venv), the Docker CLI + buildx + compose plugins, Node.js 22 + corepack/pnpm, and a pre-installed plugin set; JCasC is enabled via `CASC_JENKINS_CONFIG=/var/jenkins_home/casc.yml`.
nodes.languageNotes: Bakes Ansible + Docker CLI + Node.js into the Jenkins image so build jobs have everything they need without spinning up secondary agent containers.

nodes.name: plugins.txt
nodes.summary: Declarative Jenkins plugin manifest baked into the image at build time: JCasC, git/github, workflow/pipeline, credentials, ssh-agent, job-dsl, docker-workflow, ansicolor, junit, and prometheus.

nodes.name: casc.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Jenkins Configuration-as-Code (JCasC) template defining Jenkins entirely declaratively — credentials, jobs (DSL or pipeline definitions), security, and tool config — rendered to `/var/jenkins_home/casc.yml` and re-read after the `restart jenkins` handler fires.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutating state through the Jenkins UI is anti-pattern in this repo — anything not in this template gets overwritten on the next playbook run.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose template running the locally-built `jenkins-ansible:latest` image, bind-mounting `docker.sock` and JENKINS_HOME, with `group_add` set to the host's docker GID and Traefik labels for HTTPS ingress on the jenkins host.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Default variables for the monitoring role — defines monitoring_dir (typically /opt/monitoring) consumed by every monitoring task.

nodes.name: fleet-hosts.json
nodes.summary: Grafana dashboard showing fleet-wide host health (CPU, RAM, disk, network) for both VPS hosts derived from node_exporter metrics scraped via Prometheus.
nodes.languageNotes: Pre-built Grafana dashboard JSON with 18 top-level config sections (templating, annotations, panels).

nodes.name: home.json
nodes.summary: Landing-page Grafana dashboard summarising overall infrastructure health with cross-links to fleet, services, logs, and meta dashboards.

nodes.name: logs.json
nodes.summary: Loki-backed log explorer dashboard with container/host filters and structured-metadata search across the observability fleet.

nodes.name: meta.json
nodes.summary: Meta-observability dashboard tracking the observability pipeline itself — Alloy, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo internal metrics (scrape duration, ingestion rates, queue depths).

nodes.name: services-red.json
nodes.summary: RED-method (Rate/Errors/Duration) Grafana dashboard for application services like miplata-api and categorizer-api driven by Traefik request metrics and traces.

nodes.name: node_exporter.service
nodes.summary: Systemd unit for node_exporter running directly on the main VPS host (not containerized), with --collector.textfile.directory pointing at /var/lib/node_exporter/textfile for custom metrics.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Handlers for the monitoring role: restart_monitoring (docker compose restart), restart_node_exporter (systemd), and reload_prometheus (POST /-/reload hot-reload).

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Provisions the full observability stack on the main VPS — renders Prometheus/Loki/Alloy/Tempo/Grafana/Alertmanager configs, brings up the docker-compose stack, and installs node_exporter as a host binary plus systemd unit.
nodes.languageNotes: 30 tasks including legacy-cleanup steps for Promtail (superseded by Alloy) and orphaned dashboard files.

nodes.name: alertmanager.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Alertmanager configuration template — deployed but deliberately non-critical (notification disabled); Prometheus tolerates downtime and a soft AlertmanagerDown rule monitors it.

nodes.name: alloy-config.alloy.j2
nodes.summary: Grafana Alloy pipeline for the main VPS — scrapes containers/host metrics, tails Docker logs into Loki with JSON parsing for known emitters, and exports OTLP traces to Tempo with tail sampling.
nodes.languageNotes: Alloy's River-based DSL; every metric scrape funnels through prometheus.relabel.drop_noise to strip high-cardinality series before they reach Prometheus.

nodes.name: blackbox.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Blackbox exporter probe definitions for synthetic HTTP/HTTPS/TCP/ICMP checks against the public hostnames served by Traefik.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose stack for the full main-VPS observability plane — Prometheus, Loki, Grafana, Alloy, Tempo (conditional), cAdvisor, process-exporter, blackbox-exporter, and Alertmanager — wired into the proxy network with Traefik bearer-token-auth ingress for prom-push and loki-push.
nodes.languageNotes: Bearer-token middleware (obs-bearer) declared on Loki labels and reused by Prometheus push router; Tempo block is gated on enable_tracing.

nodes.name: grafana-provisioning-dashboards.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Grafana dashboards provider config — points at /etc/grafana/dashboards with foldersFromFilesStructure so each subdirectory becomes a UI folder.

nodes.name: grafana-provisioning-datasources.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Grafana datasource provisioning declaring Prometheus, Loki, and (when tracing is enabled) Tempo with derivedFields that link log lines back to traces via the trace_id field.
nodes.languageNotes: Configures trace-to-logs and trace-to-metrics correlation; derivedFields regex extracts trace_id from both Pino (JSON) and Python stdlib (logfmt) emitters.

nodes.name: grafana.ini.j2
nodes.summary: Grafana server config (root_url, anonymous auth disabled, security headers) rendered into /etc/grafana/grafana.ini with vault-sourced admin credentials.

nodes.name: loki-config.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Loki single-binary configuration with TSDB schema, structured-metadata support (Loki 3+), and retention/compaction tuned for a small-VPS deployment.

nodes.name: process-exporter.yml.j2
nodes.summary: process-exporter group definitions that classify host processes (sshd, docker, ansible, etc.) into named groups for Prometheus.

nodes.name: prometheus-rules.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Prometheus alerting and recording rules covering host health, container restarts, certificate expiry, scrape-target up-ness, Alloy pipeline health, and Tempo ingestion — hot-reloaded via the reload_prometheus handler.
nodes.languageNotes: 288 lines of PromQL rule groups; AlertmanagerDown is intentionally soft-severity.

nodes.name: prometheus.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Prometheus server config — global scrape interval, exemplar storage enabled, rule directory mount, alertmanager static target, and self-scrape only (Alloy ships everything else via remote_write).

nodes.name: tempo.yaml.j2
nodes.summary: Tempo single-binary configuration with OTLP gRPC/HTTP receivers, local-blocks storage, and metrics-generator producing service-graph and span metrics scraped by Prometheus.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Defaults for the observability_agent role — sets observability_agent_dir / host paths used on the Jenkins VPS.

nodes.name: node_exporter.service
nodes.summary: Systemd unit for node_exporter running on the Jenkins VPS host (not containerized) — identical structure to the main-VPS unit; metrics are scraped locally by Alloy and pushed cross-VPS.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Handlers for the observability_agent role: restart_observability_agent (docker compose restart) and restart_node_exporter (systemd).

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: Provisions the Jenkins-host observability agent — renders Alloy + docker-compose, brings up the small Alloy/cAdvisor stack, and installs node_exporter as a host binary that Alloy scrapes locally before pushing to the main VPS.

nodes.name: alloy-config.alloy.j2
nodes.summary: Jenkins-host Alloy pipeline — discovers containers via Docker SD, tails logs into Loki, scrapes node_exporter and cAdvisor for host/container metrics, then pushes everything cross-internet to the main VPS's loki-push / prom-push endpoints with bearer-token auth.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the main-VPS drop_noise discipline but uses loki.write.remote / prometheus.remote_write targeting Traefik-protected push endpoints.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml.j2
nodes.summary: Docker Compose stack for the Jenkins-host observability agent — only Alloy + cAdvisor (no Prometheus/Loki/Grafana, since data is pushed to the main VPS).

nodes.name: health-check.yml
nodes.summary: Post-deploy assertion playbook for the main VPS — verifies UFW/fail2ban/Docker, every expected container (Traefik, Vaultwarden, PowerDNS, Zot, Prometheus, Loki, Grafana, Alloy, cAdvisor, blackbox, Miplata, Metabase, llama-server, Categorizer), TLS endpoints, bearer-token auth on push endpoints, scrape target up-ness, DNS, and exposed ports.
nodes.languageNotes: Idempotent assertions; Miplata/Metabase/Categorizer/llama-server checks are gated on image presence (mirrors the role's tolerate-missing-image bootstrap pattern).

nodes.name: jenkins-health-check.yml
nodes.summary: Post-deploy assertion playbook for the Jenkins VPS — verifies firewall/Docker, Jenkins/Alloy/cAdvisor containers, node_exporter unit, Jenkins TLS, and round-trips into the main VPS's Prometheus to confirm up{host="jenkins"}==1 (cross-VPS push is actually landing).

layers.name: Orchestration & Entry Points
layers.description: Top-level Ansible playbooks, inventory, runtime config, lint rules, and Galaxy requirements that drive every deploy against the two VPS hosts.

layers.name: CI/CD Pipeline
layers.description: Jenkins-driven delivery pipeline plus the Ansible role that builds and runs the Jenkins controller image (JCasC, Dockerfile, plugins, compose) on the dedicated CI host.

layers.name: Shared Configuration & Secrets
layers.description: Cross-host variables, per-host overrides, and the ansible-vault encrypted secrets file (plus its template) consumed by every playbook and role.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Human- and agent-facing project documentation: the README overview and the CLAUDE.md guide describing repo topology, conventions, and gotchas.

layers.name: Foundation Roles
layers.description: Host-prep roles applied first on every VPS: OS hardening (UFW, fail2ban, SSH) and Docker Engine installation that all other roles depend on.

layers.name: Edge & Networking
layers.description: Public-facing perimeter: Traefik reverse proxy with ACME TLS owning ports 80/443 and the PowerDNS authoritative server that publishes A records for every other service.

layers.name: Application Services
layers.description: Compose-based application stacks deployed behind Traefik: Vaultwarden, the Miplata personal-finance app and its AI categorizer, the llm_inference llama-server, the Zot OCI registry, and Metabase BI.

layers.name: Observability
layers.description: Monitoring stack on the main VPS (Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Grafana, Alloy, cAdvisor, blackbox, dashboards) and the lightweight Alloy + node_exporter agent on the Jenkins host that pushes metrics and logs back over the internet.

layers.name: Health Checks
layers.description: Post-deploy verification playbooks executed after every CI deploy to assert that the main VPS and Jenkins host are functionally healthy.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the human- and agent-facing documentation. README.md introduces the two-VPS layout — a public web host behind Traefik + Let's Encrypt and a separate Jenkins host that builds container images and deploys back to it. CLAUDE.md goes deeper into repo conventions, role ordering constraints, and the gotchas (vault file is encrypted, .vault_pass is gitignored, role order in the playbook matters) you need to keep in mind for every step that follows.

tour.title: Entry Points & Inventory
tour.description: Both deploys are orchestrated by a flat Ansible playbook. playbook.yml drives the main VPS through eleven roles in a deliberately dependency-sensitive order; jenkins-playbook.yml drives the CI host through a smaller baseline plus the Jenkins role. inventory.yml is the connective tissue: two hosts whose ansible_host values come from the encrypted vault, so the repo is safe to publish. Read these three side-by-side and the rest of the project becomes a tree of roles hanging off them.
tour.languageLesson: Ansible playbooks have no implicit dependency resolution — the order in the `roles:` list IS the execution order. Reordering can silently break things (e.g. a role joining the `proxy` Docker network before `traefik` created it).

tour.title: Shared Config & Secrets
tour.description: Configuration is layered. group_vars/all.yml is the single source of truth for non-secret shared values — image pins, hostnames, Docker network names, UFW rule sets, observability ports. host_vars/{vps,jenkins}.yml override per-host details (the Jenkins host uses `root` as ssh user and a different UFW set). vault.yml is AES256-encrypted and holds every identifying value (IP, domain, ACME email, tokens); vault.yml.example is the unencrypted template for onboarding. ansible.cfg ties them together — fact caching on, sudo on, vault password auto-loaded from .vault_pass.
tour.languageLesson: Ansible variable precedence: role defaults < group_vars/all < group_vars/<group> < host_vars/<host> < extra vars. Putting service tunables in group_vars/all.yml and identifying info in vault.yml is the standard split for a publishable IaC repo.

tour.title: Foundation: Host Hardening & Docker
tour.description: The first two roles run on every host. The base role installs core packages, applies SSH hardening, configures UFW (including a narrow rule allowing Docker bridge subnets 172.16.0.0/12 to reach node_exporter on :9100), enables unattended-upgrades, and tunes fail2ban. The docker role idempotently adds the Docker apt repo (guarded by a `docker --version` probe), installs the engine + compose v2 plugin, and pre-creates the shared `proxy` and `miplata_db` networks. Nothing downstream can run until both have completed.

tour.title: Edge Layer: Traefik & PowerDNS
tour.description: Building on the Docker networks from Step 4, the edge layer owns everything user-facing. Traefik binds ports 80/443, terminates TLS via ACME HTTP-01 (acme.json chmod 0600), and exposes every other service by Compose labels on the shared `proxy` network. PowerDNS runs as a container on the same VPS and is authoritative for the project domain — downstream roles register their A records with `docker exec pdns pdnsutil replace-rrset` (note: short relative name, not FQDN). Traefik's compose template has the highest fan-in of any service in the repo — eight downstream roles plug into it.
tour.languageLesson: Jinja2 templates with the `.j2` extension are rendered by Ansible's `template` module, substituting variables from group_vars/host_vars/vault at deploy time. This is why compose files are templated (not copied): vault secrets and per-host config resolve into them.

tour.title: Application Stack: Miplata + AI Pipeline
tour.description: The headline app. Miplata is a pnpm/turbo monorepo (NestJS API + nginx web + Postgres + Redis) deployed as a Compose stack joined to both `proxy` (Traefik) and `miplata_db` (isolated DB plane). Crucially, the Ansible role does NOT build images — they come from the Zot registry, populated by the Jenkins job in Step 9. That's why `docker compose pull` is tolerantly handled (`failed_when: false`) and `up` is guarded by `when: miplata_pull.rc == 0`. The categorizer is the AI sidecar that consumes transactions via pgvector, calling the llm_inference llama-server over a private network for chat completions. Vaultwarden and Zot round out the stack as supporting tenants behind Traefik.

tour.title: Analytics & Registry: Metabase + Zot
tour.description: Two supporting services round out the application plane. Metabase is the BI tool that queries Postgres through the read-only `metabase_ro` role the miplata task provisions — out-of-app analytics without granting write access. Zot is the self-hosted OCI registry that holds the images the Jenkins pipeline pushes to and the Miplata/categorizer roles pull from. Both attach to `proxy` for TLS termination and register their own PowerDNS A records on apply.

tour.title: Observability: Push From Jenkins to Main VPS
tour.description: This is the non-obvious topology. The full stack — Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Grafana, Alloy, cAdvisor, blackbox, process-exporter — runs as containers on the main VPS. The Jenkins host doesn't host Prom or Loki; instead, observability_agent installs Alloy + node_exporter and PUSHES metrics and logs over the public internet to `prom-push.<web_subdomain>` and `loki-push.<web_subdomain>`, which Traefik exposes with bearer-token auth (`vault_observability_push_token`). node_exporter on the main VPS runs as a systemd unit on the host (not a container), which is why the base role's UFW rule has to open :9100 to the Docker bridge ranges.
tour.languageLesson: Alloy uses HCL-like `.alloy` config files (formerly Grafana Agent flow mode). Components are wired by export references — e.g. `prometheus.remote_write.main.receiver` is consumed by scrape components — which lets one agent unify metrics, logs, and traces.

tour.title: CI/CD: Jenkins on Jenkins
tour.description: On the Jenkins VPS, the jenkins role builds a local image (`jenkins-ansible:latest`) from a Dockerfile that grafts in Ansible (in a venv), the Docker CLI + buildx + compose plugin, and Node 22 + pnpm — everything its pipelines need to build apps like Miplata. It then runs Jenkins via Compose with `docker.sock` bind-mounted and `group_add` set to the host's docker GID (discovered at deploy time). Config is fully declarative via JCasC (casc.yml.j2) — touching the UI is futile, the next playbook run will overwrite it. The Jenkinsfile is the meta-pipeline that runs against THIS repo: galaxy install → ansible-lint → syntax check → `--check --diff` dry run → real deploy → health-check.
tour.languageLesson: Mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` into a container gives that container root-equivalent control of the host. Jenkins needs it to build images, but the trade-off is that any pipeline running in this Jenkins can spawn host containers. The `group_add` trick aligns the in-container Jenkins user with the host's docker group so it can talk to the socket without running as root.

tour.title: Verification: Health Checks
tour.description: Every CI deploy ends here. tests/health-check.yml asserts the main VPS state functionally — Traefik is up, every expected service responds on its hostname, PowerDNS resolves, observability endpoints answer — using the same role/group_vars context as the deploy itself. tests/jenkins-health-check.yml mirrors that for the CI host. Both mirror the Miplata `pull-may-fail-on-cold-start` guard so they don't false-positive on a fresh VPS where images don't yet exist. Run them locally after any deploy; the Jenkinsfile runs them automatically on every push to main.
